sourceFindings.finding: Initial list/watch checks call authorize for each admitted binding. Existing15s heartbeat checks credential ID and ServerVersion, without an evident repeat list/watch SSAR for unchanged credentials. This source observation is not a runtime bug verdict or a claim about live Kubernetes established-watch authorization.

Emit gate checks ready/watchFailed, but queued-data dispatch sends directly. Terminal authorization failure must not be merely enqueued behind resource data or depend on select prioritizing a failure channel.

minimalDesign.scope: Only active resource-watch consumer authorization refresh; no endpoint/UI-loop/framework change.
minimalDesign.schedule: Reuse existing15s heartbeat and single writer loop; no SSAR per informer event/message.
minimalDesign.budget: Create one context.WithTimeout(ctx,5s) for the entire refresh batch, cancel once after all checks. Do not allocate5s per binding. Sequential work stops on first denial/error/deadline. Network and SSAR run outside emit gate/operator/broker locks.
minimalDesign.checkSet: Snapshot/de-duplicate the already-admitted active bindings by scope.key/GVR/namespace. Check both list and watch for every required active scope, using binding Group/Resource and effective namespace, never Kind or only the first scope. Preserve version in scope identity. Normalize * to all-namespace only where existing workspace rules allow it; explicit multi-namespace scopes remain explicit. Do not silently skip a scope or publish partial green when the total deadline/quota is exhausted.
minimalDesign.authorizationReuse: Use existing authorize read semantics and existing namespace expansion, or a narrow helper with equivalent attributes. Treat denied Allowed and SSAR call errors separately; a successful HTTP response alone is not permission. Avoid broad cluster-UID authorization caches.
minimalDesign.writerBarrier: While synchronous heartbeat authorization is pending, the sole writer does not drain queued resource messages. On denial/error set consumer-local terminal state/ready=false/watchFailed=true under a short gate lock, copy failed scope metadata and unlock. Send direct terminal STATUS without resource payload, then return/cancel. Do not put failure status behind out. Make queued dispatch consult local failed/cancelled state before resource-send admission; no extra network call per message. Already in-flight bytes cannot be recalled, and no zero-delay revocation guarantee is claimed.
minimalDesign.status: Synced/SnapshotReady false; failed scope Authoritative=false; forbidden for explicit permission/auth denial, unavailable for timeout/transport/error, with safe error and GVR/namespace. Cached data is stale, not deletion or OUT_OF_SCOPE evidence. Report Reachable according to observed failure instead of treating ServerVersion success as RBAC authority.
minimalDesign.livenessProbe: Do authorization before any optional ServerVersion call, or reuse successful checks as liveness; a context-free ServerVersion must not defeat the declared whole-check budget.
minimalDesign.cleanup: Return through existing consumer defers: cancel context, remove event handlers and release broker subscription. Do not indiscriminately close a shared informer used by an independently authorized peer; last-reference release stops it. Keep workspace membership generation guards.
minimalDesign.capacityAndCost: For N distinct admitted scope/namespace checks, at most2N reviews per refresh per consumer (plus existing explicit namespace expansion where applicable); nominal average about2N/15 requests/s. Deduplicate and use existing admission limits; if not all required checks fit the fixed request/time budget, close as unavailable. Cost is network/API-server and some Go work; neither CPU impact nor latency/energy savings was measured.

existingIsolation.credentialVsRBAC: Operator reset/cancellation and credential-generation rotation already revoke grants/streams; unchanged credential with changed RoleBinding is a separate refresh question.
existingIsolation.broker: workspace_broker.go31/40 keys on client ID plus GVR/namespace. c.ID/connection generation, not common physical cluster UID, must bind sharing and any auth result reuse. Different credentials cannot borrow another consumer permission/cache authority. release77 cancels only at last listener.
existingIsolation.membership: workspace_membership.go21/37/62 binds updates and previous-member cache to stream generation; failure is not proof of Kubernetes object deletion.

separatePathLimits.limit: Start checks pods/log and pod get/watch; UID/membership watch/read guards exist. Those are not proven periodic renewal of established pods/log permission.
Start create pods/exec and UID checks, then context-bound SPDY stream. Operator cancel does not itself establish periodic unchanged-credential RBAC refresh.
Creation/request identity and authorization plus context termination exist; an already-established forwarded stream needs separate review for permission changes.
Request-time scope authorization and credential-bound leases exist. Underlying provider/lease revocation timing is a separate question; no instant-revoke inference.

cases: Positive: unchanged permissions survive next heartbeat and controlled event still arrives with same scoped generation.

Deny: keep fake upstream watch available, change one required list OR watch review to denied, queue a controlled marker while batch is pending; after known denial no queued marker reaches client, terminal non-authoritative scope status and consumer close occur.
Error/timeout: SSAR transport/error/hanging review fails closed within one total batch deadline across multiple scopes; no per-binding time multiplication and no terminal resource payload.
Cleanup/isolation: removed handlers, cancelled consumer and release occur exactly once; authorized sibling credential/scope is not closed or lent authority; last subscriber stops shared watch.

laterOwnedRealE2E: Separate explicitly authorized ServiceAccount/Role/RoleBinding+namespace+synthetic resources, verify live SSAR allow, remove the exact owned RoleBinding and observe live SSAR deny/upstream watch behavior independently, then gateway stale/close and cleanup by owner/UID/RV. Do not assume a fake server proves API-server watch authorization semantics.
acceptanceLimits: Source-only risk; root assigns severity after repro and exposure review.
No runtime bug/PASS, implementation, regression execution, real-cluster or established-session revocation acceptance in this job.
Local-first single-operator model retained; no expansion into multi-tenant identity claims.
operations: Source reads and three new design artifacts only; no tests/app/browser/build/agents/Git/index/ROADMAP/product writes.
